title: Ethical and Social Issues Around Data Collection

questions.question: A survey samples only app users to estimate all students' access to phones. What is the concern?
questions.explanation: Students without app access are excluded from the sample.

questions.question: Which best reduces risk if student records leak?

options.value: Collect fewer identifiers and limit retention

questions.explanation: Data minimization limits exposure of unnecessary personal details.

questions.question: What does anonymization attempt to remove?
questions.explanation: Anonymization reduces identification risk, though combinations of fields can still reveal identity.

questions.question: Can removing names alone guarantee anonymity?

options.value: No, other fields may identify a person

questions.explanation: Combining location, age, and other attributes can permit re-identification.

questions.question: What should users know before contributing personal data?

options.value: The purpose, use, and sharing of the data

questions.question: Which is a risk of a nonrepresentative training data set?
questions.explanation: A model may not generalize well to underrepresented groups.

questions.question: What should a report do with uncertainty?

options.value: Treat it as proof of causation
Describe it and avoid unsupported conclusions

questions.explanation: Responsible interpretation communicates limits of the evidence.

questions.question: Two measurements are correlated. What follows?

options.value: Causation is not established by correlation alone

questions.explanation: Confounding factors or chance can explain a relationship.

questions.question: What is a good retention policy?

options.value: Keep data only as long as needed for an agreed purpose

questions.explanation: A retention limit reduces exposure and respects the collection purpose.

questions.question: Who should access sensitive student records?

options.value: Only authorized people with a legitimate need

questions.question: A public data set has a license. What must a developer do?

options.value: Assume all commercial use is allowed
Ignore it because it is public

questions.explanation: Public access and unrestricted reuse are different.

questions.question: Why record the source and collection date?

options.value: To guarantee the values are correct
To assess context, reliability, and relevance

questions.explanation: Provenance helps evaluate whether data fits the question.

questions.question: A dashboard hides unfavorable observations. What is the issue?
questions.explanation: Omitting relevant observations can distort conclusions.

questions.question: Which collection choice respects privacy?

options.value: Use aggregated counts when individual records are unnecessary

questions.explanation: Aggregate data can meet a need with less personal exposure.

questions.question: A consent form permits research only. Can the data automatically be sold for advertising?

options.value: Yes, if the file is small
No, that is a different use requiring appropriate authorization

questions.explanation: Secondary use must respect the agreed purpose and permissions.

questions.question: What should happen after discovering a data error that changes a published result?

options.value: Ignore the error if the chart looks good
Correct the data and communicate the revised result

questions.explanation: Accountable analysis corrects significant mistakes transparently.
